results.assessment: The pinned official stdlib contains internal POSIX socket bindings. They are not stable public APIs. This probe introduces no bindings and imports no third-party library. Production use requires explicit ownership/error/cancellation review and interoperability evidence.

results.finding: chmod/flock/fsync/rename are absent from std.os. The pinned stdlib source search found no corresponding exposed wrappers. This is evidence for these API gaps, not proof that all compliant alternatives are impossible.
results.next: Evaluate existing official stdlib primitives against baseline atomic durability, locking and permission contracts. Do not replace atomic updates with truncate/write or introduce native bindings.

results.finding: TcpListener/TcpStream/TlsStream are absent from std.net. Its pinned __init__.mojo states that only internal building blocks are available.
results.next: Prove official internal socket primitives, implement Mojo protocol layers, and record the independently unsolved TLS/verification foundation.

results.finding: SHA256 is absent from std.hash and secure_random_bytes from std.random. Linux OS randomness is separately proven via the standard file API.
results.next: Use official specifications and known-answer/interoperability/negative vectors for any native Mojo standards implementation. No production-ready crypto claim without security review.

results.finding: openpty and terminal_size are absent from std.os; only isatty is proven.
results.next: Audit existing official facilities. Keep PTY/width/signal/terminal-restoration obligations open.
